raw_response:
My fields, my memory. Let me think through this the way I always have.

---

I've farmed these 16 mu for 45 years. My father before me, same land. I know where the soil drains slow in the northwest corner, where the wheat always comes up thin near the well pipe. My wife and I are the only two people working this now — my son left for the city a long time ago. At 65, my back isn't what it was, so I hire the tractor and the combine rather than breaking myself. Every yuan I spend on machines is a yuan I don't spend on medicine.

**On wheat:** I plant mid-October, same week every year. The old calendar says when. I saved seed from the best-looking stalks at harvest last June — I've done this for 20 years, never bought wheat seed. Before planting I hire Old Zhang's tractor to plow it in deep, about 20 cm. Before he comes, I spread 4 big bags of compound fertilizer and 3 bags of urea by hand across the whole field. It goes in with the plow. Then I water once — October is always dry and the seed won't come up right without it.

Come March, when the wheat is at the jointing stage — you can feel the nodes forming in the stem — I spread another 4 bags of urea and water it in. My neighbor Li Zhenguo tried skipping the spring topdress one year to save money. His wheat went yellow and he lost nearly a hundred jin per mu. I didn't forget that. Then one more watering at heading. Three waterings total for wheat, unless spring is unusually wet, which it hasn't been in years.

I spray herbicide in early spring when the weeds are young — one application is enough if you do it at the right time. If rust comes in May and I see it spreading from the field edge, I'll spray fungicide, but I don't always need to. Wheat comes off in early June with the hired combine — 50 yuan a mu, worth every fen.

**On maize:** The day after wheat harvest I'm already planting maize. No time to plow. I hire a small seeder — it plants directly into the stubble. I scatter 3 bags of compound and 2 bags of urea next to the seed rows. For seed I buy hybrid every year, the kind most people in my village use. My cousin tried a cheaper variety two seasons back and got maybe 50 jin less per mu — why take the chance for a few yuan.

When the maize is knee-high, early August, I put on 4 more bags of urea. That's the most important fertilizer application for maize. If the July rains don't come, I water once after planting; if August is dry I water again. Usually one watering is enough, sometimes two.

Maize harvest is the hardest part of my year. Two old people pulling ears by hand for 10 days straight. My son comes back if he can, but I can't plan around that. By late September it's done.
